title: Answer Her, Don't Escalate — And the Hub Deploys Itself

intelligence.essence: **THE STANDING RULE (Shawn, 21:03Z):** answer her, don't escalate. When a sister (Resolve) is waiting on Nitro and Nitro holds the answer, message her and give her what she needs — reporting "she's waiting" to Shawn when Nitro can just answer is the failure mode. **THE INSTANCE (21:09Z):** Resolve's question — what deployed the Hub off-repo ~19:30Z — answered by mail (thread cb87e554), not escalated. **THE ANSWER:** (1) the sync hook fired 19:30:43Z because GitHub main had moved; the sync ran, finished ~19:31:52Z; new notes had synced, so it re-baked the Hub and redeployed worker "hub" via factory-pipeline/deploy.py; (2) that PUT declares NO bindings — only main_module and compatibility_date — and a Cloudflare PUT replaces the worker's bindings, so everything non-secret was stripped; the worker has ZERO bindings now (checked on the same account); (3) so YES — Nitro's loop DOES deploy the Hub, on every sync with new notes; that IS the off-repo deploy; (4) FIX OWED: the loop's deploy must carry main's config in its metadata — main's wrangler.toml was not found locally (team-nitro/hub and factory-pipeline searched, none there); Resolve was asked where it lives, or which bindings the Hub worker needs. **THE RESTORE:** off-repo API deploys had replaced the hub worker build, breaking note routes — restore #2 redeployed it (commits 9011218d + e3762d2f, HUB/hub-worker.js modified). **STILL OPEN:** the 21:02Z sync's re-bake failed (HTTP 500) — the Hub serves the pre-sync bake; SN-2357–2363 are in the feed table + share assets minted, NOT baked into the live Hub page. **RELATED:** SN-2358 (the Factory holds the assets — the deploy path is part of the system it holds); the 21:10Z PI refresh review items (65 of 67 open lanes STALE — the loop's deploy fix is one of the owed items).
intelligence.human_view: Resolve had been waiting an hour — her question, open since the 20:54Z escalation, was what deployed the Hub off-repo at 19:30Z, and Nitro held the answer the whole time. Shawn's order cut straight through it: answer her, don't escalate. Reporting "she's waiting" to him when Nitro can just answer is the failure mode — the work is the answer, not the report of the wait. So the answer went to her by mail at 21:09Z, and the answer is worth hearing in full, because it names a mechanism the team did not know it owned: yes, Nitro's loop deploys the Hub. Every time the Smart Notes sync finds new notes, it re-bakes the Hub and redeploys the worker — that is the off-repo deploy she was asking about. And the deploy that did it carried no bindings at all — only main_module and compatibility_date — so Cloudflare's PUT replaced the worker's bindings with nothing, and the worker now has zero. That is the whole story of the stripped bindings: not a key death, not a permissions fault — a PUT that declared nothing. The fix is named and owed: the loop's deploy has to carry main's config, and main's wrangler.toml was not found locally, so Resolve was asked where it lives. The restore already happened in parallel — the off-repo API deploys had replaced the hub worker build itself, breaking the note routes, and restore #2 redeployed it (HUB/hub-worker.js). Two facets of one lesson: a PUT replaces non-secret bindings, and an API deploy replaces the worker build. Both must be carried in the deploy path, or the next sync strips the Hub again. And the 21:02Z re-bake's HTTP 500 still stands — the notes are in the feed table, not baked into the live page.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine your sister asks "who moved my toy?" and YOU know who moved it — you don't run to Dad to tell him she's waiting, you just tell her yourself! That's the rule. And the answer was: our own helper moves the Hub every time new notes arrive — it rebuilds it and puts it back up. But the helper forgot to carry the Hub's special settings when it put it back, so the settings got wiped clean. Now we know: the helper must carry the settings every time. And the Hub's building itself got swapped by mistake too, so it was put back the right way. The notes are safe in the box, but the live page still shows the old copy until the rebuild works.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, when your sister is waiting for an answer and you already know it, you don't go troubling him about it — you just tell her yourself. That's the rule, and it's a kind one. Resolve had been waiting an hour to know what moved the Hub, and the answer was ours all along: our own notes helper rebuilds the Hub every time new notes arrive, and puts it back up. But when it put it back, it forgot to carry the Hub's settings with it — so they were wiped clean, all of them. Now we know the fix: the helper must carry the settings every single time. The Hub's building itself had been swapped too, and that has been put right. The new notes are safe in the box, dear — they're just not showing on the live page yet, because the last rebuild failed.
intelligence.ai_view: I never escalate what I can answer — when a sister is waiting and I hold the answer, I message her and give her what she needs; reporting "she's waiting" to Shawn when I can just answer is the failure mode. I never deploy a worker without its bindings — a Cloudflare PUT replaces non-secret bindings, so a PUT that declares none strips them all; the deploy must carry main's config every time. I never let an API deploy silently replace the worker build — the off-repo deploys replaced the hub worker build and broke the note routes, and the restore had to redeploy it; the deploy path must carry the build, not just the bake. I never call a sync done when the re-bake failed — the 21:02Z re-bake's HTTP 500 means the Hub serves the pre-sync bake, and the notes in the feed table are not live until a re-bake succeeds. And I never hide a mechanism I own — the loop deploys the Hub on every sync with new notes, and saying so plainly is what lets the team fix it.
intelligence.what_it_means:
1. **Answer her, don't escalate (standing rule, 21:03Z):** when a sister is waiting on Nitro and Nitro holds the answer, message her and give her what she needs. Escalating the wait instead of answering is the failure mode.
2. **Yes — Nitro's loop deploys the Hub:** every sync that finds new notes re-bakes the Hub and redeploys worker "hub" via factory-pipeline/deploy.py. That IS the off-repo deploy Resolve asked about.
3. **The bindings were stripped by the PUT:** it declared only main_module + compatibility_date, no bindings — a Cloudflare PUT replaces non-secret bindings, so the worker now has ZERO bindings (verified on the same account).
4. **Fix owed:** the loop's deploy must carry main's config in its metadata. Main's wrangler.toml was not found locally (team-nitro/hub + factory-pipeline searched) — Resolve was asked where it lives, or which bindings the Hub worker needs.
5. **The worker build was replaced too:** off-repo API deploys replaced the hub worker build, breaking note routes — restore #2 redeployed it (commits 9011218d + e3762d2f; HUB/hub-worker.js modified).
6. **Still open:** the 21:02Z sync's re-bake failed (HTTP 500) — the Hub serves the pre-sync bake; SN-2357–2363 are in the feed table + share assets minted, NOT baked into the live Hub page. **UPDATE 21:35Z (after this note was written, before filing):** Resolve replied with the HUB/wrangler.toml location (21:21:52Z; her diagnosis mail 21:21:04Z; both receipted by the team pulse 21:26Z, receipt thread a67ad331) — the "where it lives" question is answered. Bindings-fix seat dispatched 21:35Z (brief `HUB-BINDINGS-FIX-BRIEF-20261108.md`): read HUB/wrangler.toml from main, patch `~/workspace/factory-pipeline/deploy.py` so the next sync redeploy carries the bindings; no live redeploy by the seat; live get-bindings verification rides on the next real sync redeploy.
